answer: A staking bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a deposit before it can trade or vote, and the bond is slashed when peers prove fraud. Like a willow bending in a gale, honest agents flex and survive, while a walnut-hard shell of collateral means an attacker must pay for every copy they spawn. One real identity costs little; a thousand fakes cost a thousand bonds, so sybil farming stops paying.
